sections.content: When most people think of Green Bay, Wisconsin, they think of the Packers. But savvy real estate investors are discovering something else entirely: a market full of affordable properties, steady rental demand, and genuine opportunity. Whether you're a seasoned wholesaler or just getting started — if you're new to investing, check out our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide first — Green Bay deserves a serious look. This article breaks down everything you need to know about finding real estate deals in Green Bay WI, from the neighborhoods worth targeting to the numbers that actually make sense.
Green Bay WI Real Estate Market Overview

Green Bay is the third-largest city in Wisconsin, with a metro population of around 320,000 people. It sits along the western shore of Green Bay (the body of water), making it a regional economic hub for northeast Wisconsin. The city has a diversified economy anchored by healthcare, manufacturing, food processing, and — yes — the NFL's Green Bay Packers organization, which generates significant tourism and local spending year-round.

The housing market here has remained remarkably stable compared to volatile Sun Belt cities. Home values appreciated steadily during the post-pandemic boom but didn't experience the extreme runups seen in Phoenix or Austin. That means Green Bay didn't crash as hard either. As of 2024, the median home price in Green Bay sits around $210,000 to $230,000 — well below the national median — while average rents for a single-family home range from $1,100 to $1,600 per month depending on size and location. That combination creates real cash flow potential that many larger markets simply can't offer anymore.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Green Bay

Green Bay is a city of distinct neighborhoods, and knowing which ones pencil out for investors is half the battle. You can explore current active deals and neighborhood data at our [Green Bay WI market page](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/green-bay-wi) to see what's moving right now. Here's a breakdown of the areas worth watching.
West Side: The Bread and Butter Rental Zone

The west side of Green Bay — neighborhoods like Allouez, Howard, and the areas around Titletown — offers solid working-class housing stock at prices between $150,000 and $250,000. These are your classic 3-bed, 1-bath homes built between 1950 and 1980. Rental demand is consistently strong here because of proximity to employment centers and good school districts. Investors buying in this range at a 10–15% discount can often achieve gross rent multipliers (GRMs) under 100, which is increasingly rare in most U.S. markets.
East Side and Near East: Fix-and-Flip Territory

The near east side of Green Bay, particularly around Broadway and the older downtown corridors, contains a higher concentration of distressed properties. These are prime fix-and-flip targets. ARVs in these neighborhoods run $130,000 to $190,000 for updated homes, and acquisition prices on distressed deals can fall between $60,000 and $100,000. That spread — when you control renovation costs — can yield flips in the $25,000 to $45,000 profit range. Use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to quickly model what a specific east side property might be worth after repairs.
Ashwaubenon and De Pere: Value-Add Rentals

Just outside the city limits, the suburbs of Ashwaubenon and De Pere attract tenants who want more space and slightly better school ratings. Home prices here run $220,000 to $320,000, but rents are also higher — often $1,400 to $1,800 for a 3-bedroom. Value-add multifamily properties in these suburbs are particularly interesting for buy-and-hold investors building long-term wealth.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Green Bay WI
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling is active in Green Bay, though the market is smaller than major metros, which actually works in your favor — less competition from other wholesalers. The key is finding motivated sellers before they hit the MLS. Probate estates, tax-delinquent properties, and pre-foreclosures are the most consistent sources of wholesale inventory in this market. If you're newer to this strategy, our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide will walk you through the process step by step. Assignment fees in Green Bay typically run $8,000 to $20,000 per deal depending on the equity spread.
Fix and Flip

Green Bay's older housing stock — most of the city was built before 1970 — means there's no shortage of properties needing updates. The flip market here rewards investors who keep renovation budgets tight. Labor costs in Wisconsin are lower than coastal markets, and local contractors are generally easier to find and schedule. A typical light-to-medium rehab (cosmetic updates, new kitchen and bath) runs $25,000 to $55,000. Run your numbers before you commit using our free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to make sure your offer price protects your profit margin.
Buy-and-Hold Rentals

This is arguably where Green Bay shines brightest. The city has a large renter population — approximately 45% of households rent — driven by the university (UW-Green Bay), hospital systems (Bellin and HSHS), and manufacturing employers. Vacancy rates have stayed consistently below 5% in most neighborhoods. A well-purchased rental in the $150,000 to $200,000 range can generate $200 to $400 per month in cash flow after mortgage, taxes, insurance, and a reserve for maintenance. That's not life-changing on one property, but it compounds quickly across a small portfolio.

Pro Tip: In Green Bay, target properties within 10 minutes of Bellin Hospital or HSHS St. Vincent Hospital. Healthcare workers are among the most stable, reliable tenants in any market — and Green Bay has thousands of them looking for quality rentals near their workplace.
Green Bay Real Estate Market Trends to Watch

items: Population stability: Green Bay's population has held steady around 107,000 within city limits, with metro growth in suburbs like De Pere and Howard driving demand for quality housing.
Rising rents: Average rents have increased roughly 8–12% over the past two years as new construction has lagged behind demand, improving cash flow for existing landlords.
Low days on market: Well-priced move-in-ready homes are selling in under 30 days, which means distressed off-market deals are the clearest path to buying below market value.
Interest rate sensitivity: Like all Midwest markets, Green Bay has seen buyer pullback from higher mortgage rates, which creates more negotiating room for cash investors.
Titletown development effect: The ongoing Titletown District development near Lambeau Field has increased property values and rental demand on the west side, with more growth projected through 2026.

Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Green Bay

Green Bay is absolutely investable from out of state — many successful landlords and flippers operate here remotely. But you need the right team and the right information before you wire any money. Finding deals before they hit the open market is the single biggest advantage you can build. Learn how with our guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals), which covers direct mail, driving for dollars, and digital outreach strategies that work in mid-sized Midwest markets like Green Bay.

items: Build a local team first: Find a Green Bay-based property manager, a real estate attorney familiar with Wisconsin landlord-tenant law, and at least two general contractors before you close your first deal.

Understand Wisconsin's landlord laws: Wisconsin is considered a relatively landlord-friendly state, but you need to follow proper notice procedures. Evictions typically take 6–10 weeks if handled correctly.
Use virtual tours and inspections: Most Green Bay sellers and agents are comfortable with video walkthroughs. Hire a local home inspector and ask them to do a video call during the inspection.

Account for Wisconsin winters: Budget for furnace maintenance, roof wear, and higher vacancy risk in December through February when tenant movement slows. Add $1,500 to $2,500 annually per property for winter-related maintenance.
Analyze deals conservatively: Use a 10% vacancy rate and 10% property management fee in your underwriting even if your initial numbers look better. It keeps you from getting burned.

Network through local REIAs: The Green Bay Real Estate Investors Association hosts regular meetups. Even attending virtually as an out-of-state investor can connect you with wholesalers, agents, and contractors actively working the market.

Is Green Bay WI Right for Your Investment Strategy?

Green Bay won't make you a millionaire overnight, and it's not trying to. What it offers is something arguably more valuable: consistent, predictable returns in a stable market where the fundamentals make sense. Affordable entry prices, strong renter demand, an experienced local contractor base, and a diversified local economy make this one of the more underrated markets in the Midwest. Whether you're looking to wholesale your first deal, flip a dated colonial on the east side, or build a portfolio of cash-flowing rentals, real estate deals in Green Bay WI are worth your serious attention in 2024.
